Topics · Hard times

Is poverty a sign of weak faith?

No. Wealth as honour, poverty as disgrace: the Quran says 'Nay'. Its measure: what we do for those with less.

Part 1 of 3

﴿فَأَمَّا ٱلْإِنسَـٰنُ إِذَا مَا ٱبْتَلَىٰهُ رَبُّهُۥ فَأَكْرَمَهُۥ وَنَعَّمَهُۥ فَيَقُولُ رَبِّىٓ أَكْرَمَنِ١٥ وَأَمَّآ إِذَا مَا ٱبْتَلَىٰهُ فَقَدَرَ عَلَيْهِ رِزْقَهُۥ فَيَقُولُ رَبِّىٓ أَهَـٰنَنِ١٦ كَلَّا ۖ بَل لَّا تُكْرِمُونَ ٱلْيَتِيمَ١٧﴾

Translation of the meaning

And as for man, when his Lord tries him and [thus] is generous to him and favors him, he says, "My Lord has honored me."[1918] But when He tries him and restricts his provision, he says, "My Lord has humiliated me." No![1919] But you do not honor the orphan

Translator's notes

[1918] He is proud rather than grateful, attributing the favor to his own merit.

[1919] It is not like you imagine. Rather, Allāh tries people through prosperity and hardship and rewards both gratitude and patience with honor in the Hereafter.

Quran · Al-Fajr 89:15-17

Translation

Remove far from me falsehood and lies. Give me neither poverty nor riches. Feed me with the food that is needful for me, lest I be full, deny you, and say, ‘Who is Yahweh?’ or lest I be poor, and steal, and so dishonor the name of my God.

Original · Hebrew

שָׁ֤וְא ׀ וּֽדְבַר־כָּזָ֡ב הַרְחֵ֬ק מִמֶּ֗נִּי רֵ֣אשׁ וָ֭עֹשֶׁר אַל־תִּֽתֶּן־לִ֑י הַ֝טְרִיפֵ֗נִי לֶ֣חֶם חֻקִּֽי׃ פֶּ֥ן אֶשְׂבַּ֨ע ׀ וְכִחַשְׁתִּי֮ וְאָמַ֗רְתִּי מִ֥י יְה֫וָ֥ה וּפֶֽן־אִוָּרֵ֥שׁ וְגָנַ֑בְתִּי וְ֝תָפַ֗שְׂתִּי שֵׁ֣ם אֱלֹהָֽי׃

Proverbs · 30:8-9

World English Bible

Poverty is no sign of that, and the Quran says so in its own voice. This passage describes a person who, when comfort comes, says 'my Lord has honoured me', and when his provision is tight, says 'my Lord has humiliated me'. The reply is a single word: Nay. Wealth is not the measure of honour, and a narrow provision is not a sign of disgrace. The text answers the idea you were told.

A question for you

What did your mother's life show you about faith?

If you sayEndurance.
ThenEndurance is a form of trust, and money does not measure it.
If you sayGiving from little.
ThenThat is exactly where the passage moves next: the question put to those who have more.
If you sayThat she asked, and kept asking.
ThenAsking without stopping is not lost in the Quran's words. God is near the one who calls.

Part 2 of 3

﴿أَهُمْ يَقْسِمُونَ رَحْمَتَ رَبِّكَ ۚ نَحْنُ قَسَمْنَا بَيْنَهُم مَّعِيشَتَهُمْ فِى ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا ۚ وَرَفَعْنَا بَعْضَهُمْ فَوْقَ بَعْضٍ دَرَجَـٰتٍ لِّيَتَّخِذَ بَعْضُهُم بَعْضًا سُخْرِيًّا ۗ وَرَحْمَتُ رَبِّكَ خَيْرٌ مِّمَّا يَجْمَعُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Do they distribute the mercy of your Lord? It is We who have apportioned among them their livelihood in the life of this world and have raised some of them above others in degrees [of rank] that they may make use of one another for service. But the mercy of your Lord is better than whatever they accumulate.

Quran · Az-Zukhruf 43:32

The next passage is about how provision is shared out, and it speaks plainly. It asks whether people divide the mercy of your Lord, and says it is God who divides their livelihood among them in this life and raises some above others in rank, so that they depend on one another. Then: the mercy of your Lord is better than everything they gather. Provision is distributed, not earned as a sign of favour. And mercy, what your mother prayed for, is worth more than all that is piled up.

A question for you

What do you think weighs most before God?

If you sayWhat I have.
ThenThe verse puts what we have in a different column from mercy.
If you sayWhat I do.
ThenThe last passage measures by deeds: what we do for those who have less.
If you sayWhat is in my heart.
ThenThe heart is where the mercy your mother prayed for is received.

Part 3 of 3

﴿بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ أَرَءَيْتَ ٱلَّذِى يُكَذِّبُ بِٱلدِّينِ١ فَذَٰلِكَ ٱلَّذِى يَدُعُّ ٱلْيَتِيمَ٢ وَلَا يَحُضُّ عَلَىٰ طَعَامِ ٱلْمِسْكِينِ٣﴾

Translation of the meaning

Have you seen the one who denies the Recompense? For that is the one who drives away the orphan And does not encourage the feeding of the poor.

Quran · Al-Ma'un 107:1-3

Translation

But you do see trouble and grief. You consider it to take it into your hand. You help the victim and the fatherless.

Original · Hebrew

רָאִ֡תָה כִּֽי־אַתָּ֤ה ׀ עָ֘מָ֤ל וָכַ֨עַס ׀ תַּבִּיט֮ לָתֵ֪ת בְּיָ֫דֶ֥ךָ עָ֭לֶיךָ יַעֲזֹ֣ב חֵלֶ֑כָה יָ֝ת֗וֹם אַתָּ֤ה ׀ הָיִ֬יתָ עוֹזֵֽר׃

the Psalms · 10:14

World English Bible

A short chapter on this sets the test somewhere else. It asks about the person who denies the judgment, and gives two signs: he pushes the orphan away, and he does not urge the feeding of the poor. The measure is not how much a person has. It is what a person does about someone who has less. By that measure, a woman who shares what little she has is rich.

A question for you

By that measure, how would you describe your mother?

If you sayFaithful.
ThenThe chapter looks at what a person does. The rest is known to God.
If you sayGenerous.
ThenGenerosity from little is not lost with God.
If you sayHonoured.
ThenThat is the word of the verse that answered anyone who thought poverty was disgrace.

The same in the other books

Translation

“Defend the weak, the poor, and the fatherless. Maintain the rights of the poor and oppressed. Rescue the weak and needy. Deliver them out of the hand of the wicked.”

שִׁפְטוּ־דַ֥ל וְיָת֑וֹם עָנִ֖י וָרָ֣שׁ הַצְדִּֽיקוּ׃ פַּלְּטוּ־דַ֥ל וְאֶבְי֑וֹן מִיַּ֖ד רְשָׁעִ֣ים הַצִּֽילוּ׃

the Psalms · 82:3-4

Whoever stops his ears at the cry of the poor, he will also cry out, but shall not be heard.

אֹטֵ֣ם אָ֭זְנוֹ מִזַּעֲקַת־דָּ֑ל גַּֽם־ה֥וּא יִ֝קְרָ֗א וְלֹ֣א יֵעָנֶֽה׃

Proverbs · 21:13

World English Bible

It is the Way of Heaven to diminish superabundance, and to supplement deficiency. It is not so with the way of man. He takes away from those who have not enough to add to his own superabundance.

Chinese classics · Tao Te Ching 77.2

Tao Teh King (Legge)

Translation

What good is it, my brothers, if a man says he has faith, but has no works? Can faith save him? And if a brother or sister is naked and in lack of daily food, and one of you tells them, “Go in peace. Be warmed and filled;” yet you didn’t give them the things the body needs, what good is it? Even so faith, if it has no works, is dead in itself.

Original · Ancient Greek

Τί ὄφελος, ἀδελφοί μου, ἐὰν πίστιν λέγῃ τις ἔχειν ἔργα δὲ μὴ ἔχῃ; μὴ δύναται ἡ πίστις σῶσαι αὐτόν; ἐὰν ἀδελφὸς ἢ ἀδελφὴ γυμνοὶ ὑπάρχωσιν καὶ λειπόμενοι τῆς ἐφημέρου τροφῆς, εἴπῃ δέ τις αὐτοῖς ἐξ ὑμῶν· Ὑπάγετε ἐν εἰρήνῃ, θερμαίνεσθε καὶ χορτάζεσθε, μὴ δῶτε δὲ αὐτοῖς τὰ ἐπιτήδεια τοῦ σώματος, τί ὄφελος; οὕτως καὶ ἡ πίστις, ἐὰν μὴ ἔχῃ ἔργα, νεκρά ἐστιν καθʼ ἑαυτήν.

James · 2:14-17
